flashcards.back: Preparing external financial reports (that’s financial accounting).
Direct materials + Direct labor + Manufacturing overhead.
Selling, general, and administrative (SG&A), R&D, marketing—expensed in the period.
Indirect factory costs (e.g., factory utilities, depreciation, factory supervision, maintenance, indirect materials).
Direct materials are traceable to a specific job/unit; indirect materials are used in production but not easily traceable per unit.
Direct labor is hands-on labor traceable to jobs; indirect labor supports production (maintenance, supervision).
Revenue − Operating expenses = Operating income (no inventory/COGS).
Sales − COGS = Gross profit; Gross profit − Operating expenses = Operating income.
Sales − COGS = Gross profit; Gross profit − Operating expenses = Operating income.
COGS = Beginning Finished Goods + Cost of Goods Manufactured − Ending Finished Goods.
COGM = Beginning WIP + (Direct materials used + Direct labor + MOH) − Ending WIP.
DM used = Beginning Raw Materials + Purchases − Ending Raw Materials.
Job: custom/unique jobs (accumulate by job). Process: mass/continuous production (accumulate by process/department).
Raw Materials → Work in Process → Finished Goods → Cost of Goods Sold.
DM & DL are traced to jobs; MOH is allocated using a predetermined rate.
POHR = Estimated total MOH ÷ Estimated allocation base (e.g., DLH, MH).
Applied MOH = POHR × Actual activity (e.g., actual DLH or machine hours).
Applied MOH > Actual MOH; decrease COGS if difference is immaterial and most goods sold.
Applied MOH < Actual MOH; increase COGS if difference is immaterial and most goods sold.
Close entire difference to COGS if immaterial.
Prorate difference to WIP, FG, and COGS based on ending balances (or applied MOH in each).
Assign overhead using activities and cost drivers to improve accuracy.
1) Identify activities; 2) Create cost pools; 3) Select cost drivers; 4) Compute activity rates; 5) Assign to products/services.
When OH is large, products/services are diverse, and non-unit drivers matter.
More data/effort/cost; complexity; estimates may still be imperfect; potential resistance.
Prevention, Appraisal, Internal failure, External failure.
Costs to detect defects before delivery (inspection, testing, audits).
Costs to avoid defects (training, better design, supplier certification, process control).
Defects found before shipment (rework, scrap, downtime).
Defects found by customer (returns, warranty, recalls, lost reputation).
y = a + bX, where a = fixed cost, b = variable cost per unit, X = activity level.
b = (Cost_high − Cost_low) ÷ (X_high − X_low).
a = Total cost − (b × X) using either the high or low point.
Total cost is flat within relevant range; cost per unit decreases as volume rises.
Total cost rises proportionally with volume; cost per unit remains constant.
Total cost = fixed intercept + variable slope; cost per unit decreases with higher volume.
Both record DM and DL at actual amounts; they differ in timing of MOH (applied vs actual).
Raw Materials, Work in Process, Finished Goods.
COGM transfers costs to Finished Goods; COGS transfers costs from FG to the income statement.

quiz.question:
Classify each as Product or Period cost:
1) Factory rent $60,000
2) Sales salaries $120,000
3) Factory maintenance supplies $8,000
4) CEO salary $300,000
quiz.explanation: Factory-related items (1 and 3) are product costs; SG&A (2 and 4) are period costs.

quiz.question:
Compute DM used, COGM, and COGS.
Given: Beg RM 40, Purch 180, End RM 30, DL 120, MOH 160, Beg WIP 50, End WIP 70, Beg FG 25, End FG 35.
Job vs Process costing — which is TRUE?
options: Job costing accumulates costs by department for homogeneous products
Process costing accumulates costs by job for unique products
Job costing uses job cost sheets to track DM, DL, MOH per job
Process costing cannot use equivalent units
quiz.explanation: Job costing is for unique/custom jobs tracked on job cost sheets; process costing is department-based for homogeneous output.

quiz.question: Predetermined MOH: Estimated MOH $600,000; Estimated DLH 200,000; Actual DLH 210,000; Actual MOH $590,000. What is applied MOH and over/under?
Closing overapplied MOH (immaterial; most goods sold) should...
quiz.explanation: Overapplied means too much cost was expensed; reduce COGS to correct.

quiz.question: ABC accuracy most improves when the firm has...
options: Low OH; similar products; one unit driver
High OH; diverse products; several non-unit drivers
Low OH; diverse products; unit driver adequate
High OH; identical products; unit driver adequate
quiz.explanation: ABC is best with complex, diverse environments and large overhead tied to non-unit drivers.

quiz.question: Costs of Quality — classify: 1) Supplier certification program  2) Final inspection testing  3) Rework  4) Warranty repairs
options: Prevention, Appraisal, Internal Failure, External Failure
Appraisal, Prevention, External Failure, Internal Failure
Prevention, Internal Failure, Appraisal, External Failure
External Failure, Internal Failure, Appraisal, Prevention
quiz.explanation: 1 Prevention; 2 Appraisal; 3 Internal failure; 4 External failure.

quiz.question: High–Low Method: At 10,000 units, total cost = $85,000; at 16,000 units, total cost = $109,000. Find b and a in y=a+bX.
Predict total cost using y = 45,000 + 4X at X = 14,000 units.

Cost behavior classification:
A) Total fixed cost within relevant range
B) Variable cost per unit
C) Mixed cost per unit as volume increases
options: A increases; B increases; C increases
A constant; B constant; C decreases
A constant; B increases; C constant
A decreases; B constant; C increases
quiz.explanation: Fixed total stays constant; variable per unit constant; mixed per unit falls as fixed is spread.

quiz.question: Service vs Merch vs Manufacturing — which statement is TRUE?
options: Service firms carry RM, WIP, and FG inventories
Merchandisers compute Cost of Goods Manufactured each period
Manufacturers compute both COGM and COGS
quiz.explanation: Only manufacturers produce inventory and compute both COGM and COGS.

quiz.question: Best MOH allocation base when production is highly automated:
quiz.explanation: With automation, machine hours generally correlate better with overhead usage than direct labor hours.

questions.prompt: Factory utilities
questions.explanation: Factory-related → product cost (MOH).

questions.prompt: Sales commissions
questions.explanation: Selling costs are period costs.

questions.prompt: Depreciation on factory equipment
questions.explanation: Factory depreciation → MOH (product).

questions.prompt: CEO salary
questions.explanation: Administrative cost → period.

questions.prompt: Quality inspection before shipment
questions.explanation: Inspection/testing are appraisal costs.

questions.prompt: Supplier certification program
questions.explanation: Certification to avoid defects → prevention.

questions.prompt: Total fixed cost within the relevant range
questions.explanation: Total fixed cost is constant in the relevant range.

questions.prompt: Variable cost per unit
questions.explanation: Variable per unit is constant; total varies with volume.

questions.prompt: Mixed cost per unit as volume increases
questions.explanation: Fixed portion is spread over more units, lowering per-unit mixed cost.

questions.prompt: Best allocation base in a highly automated plant
questions.explanation: Machine hours better reflect OH usage in automation.

questions.prompt: COGS = Beginning Finished Goods + ___ − Ending Finished Goods
questions.explanation: COGS draws from FG; COGM is what was transferred into FG.

questions.prompt: COGM = Beginning WIP + (DM used + DL + ___) − Ending WIP
questions.explanation: Three manufacturing cost elements: DM, DL, MOH.

questions.prompt: Direct materials used = Beginning Raw Materials + ___ − Ending Raw Materials
questions.explanation: Purchases increase available raw materials.

questions.prompt: Predetermined MOH rate (POHR) = Estimated MOH ÷ Estimated ___
questions.explanation: Common bases: DL hours, machine hours.

questions.prompt: Applied MOH = POHR × Actual ___
questions.explanation: Apply using actual measure of the chosen base.

questions.prompt: Mixed cost model: y = a + ___ × X
questions.explanation: b is the variable rate per unit of activity.

questions.prompt: High–Low: b = (Cost_high − Cost_low) ÷ (___high − ___low)
questions.explanation: Use the high/low activity levels, not costs, in the denominator.

questions.prompt: In job costing, DM and DL are ___ to jobs, MOH is ___
questions.explanation: Traceable vs allocated is the key distinction.

questions.prompt: Four quality cost categories: Prevention, Appraisal, Internal failure, ___ failure
questions.explanation: External = costs after delivery (warranty, returns).

questions.prompt: Production inventory flow: Raw Materials → Work in Process → ___ → COGS
questions.explanation: Finished Goods precede expense recognition as COGS.
